subject: Bhagavad Gita
hook: BHAGAVAD GITA IS NOT WHAT YOU THINK
angle: The Bhagavad Gita is not the work of a single human sage, but a composite text likely authored or compiled by multiple contributors.
angle_support: While traditionally attributed to the sage Veda Vyasa, the Bhagavad Gita is historiographically regarded as a composite work by multiple authors.
According to Alexus McLeod, a scholar of Philosophy and Asian Studies, it is 'impossible to link the Bhagavad Gita to a single author', and it may be the work of many authors.
title: Who Actually Wrote the Bhagavad Gita?
description: While tradition credits the sage Vyasa, historical evidence suggests the Bhagavad Gita was a composite work. This video explores the multiple authors behind the scripture.
narration: BHAGAVAD GITA IS NOT WHAT YOU THINK You picture a single sage, Veda Vyasa, penning this masterpiece in one sitting. It was closer to a collaborative synthesis by at least three different historical contributors. Scholars identify multiple authors because the text abruptly shifts between rigid philosophical logic and intense, emotional theism. Rather than a lone writer, it is a composite work compiled over centuries, blending diverse religious strands into one epic. Tradition creates the author, but history reveals a collective voice.
